rounds.text: Steel Authority of India Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 11.1x and a price-to-book ratio of 1.07x [E1, E2]. These valuation metrics sit comfortably below sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E is 14.59x, the sector P/B is 1.86x, and the EV/EBITDA is 6.1x against a sector benchmark of 9.32x [E6, E7, E11]. Profitability is showing powerful acceleration, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 115% over the trailing twelve months and a quarterly net profit surge of 318% year-over-year [E21, E68]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded by 2 percentage points in the TTM period to reach 13%, and surged by 4 percentage points in the quarter ending September 2026 compared to the same period a year ago [E30, E31]. Cash generation is exceptionally robust, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 19,039 Cr, free cash flow hitting Rs 10,942 Cr, and a stellar cash conversion ratio of 5.64x for March 2026 indicating that reported profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35, E36]. Institutional confidence is also building as foreign institutions increased their holding to 7.30% in September 2026 from 4.34% in December 2023, while domestic institutions raised their stake to 16.49% from 15.46% over the same timeframe [E42, E43]. Conceded: [E45], [E46], [E63], [E64].

The valuation is unsupported because a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 150 per share against a market price of Rs 161, leaving a negative margin of safety of -7.2% [E45, E46]. Fundamental returns are weak and sub-par, highlighted by a low return on equity of 5.85% over the last 3 years and a 10-year median return on equity of just 7% [E26, E62], while 3-year compounded sales growth has stalled to a meager 2% [E16]. Balance sheet and risk metrics flash severe warnings, including a current ratio of 0.82x where current liabilities exceed current assets, massive contingent liabilities of Rs 43,331 Cr, and potential capitalization of interest costs [E38, E63, E64]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reached 115% and operating cash flow hit Rs 19,039 Cr [E21, E35].

The bear's reliance on a static discounted cash flow valuation at Rs 150 ignores the dramatic momentum in earnings where trailing twelve-month profit growth spiked 115% and net profit jumped 318% YoY, reflecting an accelerating turnaround that stale models miss [E21, E45, E68, E73]. Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales growth is 2% [E16], but this masks robust recent quarterly acceleration with sales up 20% YoY and operating margins expanding to 13% from 9% in the year-ago quarter [E31, E66]. While the bear cites weak 3-year ROE, structural profitability is improving as evidenced by operating margin expanding over the TTM period to 13% against 11% three years earlier [E30, E62]. On the balance sheet risk, the bear ignores that borrowings actually decreased to Rs 31,464 Cr from Rs 31,928 Cr a year earlier, and operating cash flow reached an immense Rs 19,039 Cr with profits fully backed by a 5.64x cash conversion [E35, E39]. Finally, foreign and domestic institutional holdings have increased since December 2023—with foreign institutions rising from 4.34% to 7.30%—proving that sophisticated capital is accumulating despite near-term technical friction [E42, E43].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth spiked 115% and net profit jumped 318% YoY [E21, E68]. However, dismissing the discounted cash flow valuation of ₹150 ignores the reality that the current market price of ₹161 carries a negative margin of safety of -7.2% [E2, E45, E46]. Conceded: sales are up 20% YoY and operating margins expanded to 13% in Sep 2026 [E31, E66], but this recent spike contrasts sharply with a stagnant 3-year compounded sales growth of just 2% and a poor 5-year sales growth of 9.90% [E16, E61]. Conceded: borrowings decreased to ₹31,464 Cr and cash conversion is high [E35, E39], yet the current ratio stands at a dangerous 0.82x where current liabilities exceed current assets, alongside looming contingent liabilities of ₹43,331 Cr and risks that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E38, E63, E64]. Furthermore, while the bull highlights rising institutional holdings since December 2023 [E42, E43], recent data records negative money flow with an institutional holding change of -0.17 percentage points, while the price remains below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E44, E50, E72].
